title: 1956 AHSME Problem 31
statement: In our number system the base is ten. If the base were changed to four you would count as follows: \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(10,\) \(11,\) \(12,\) \(13,\) \(20,\) \(21,\) \(22,\) \(23,\) \(30,\) \(\ldots\) The twentieth number would be:

solutions.text:
The twentieth positive integer has ordinary value \(20.\) Since \[ 20=1\cdot4^2+1\cdot4+0, \] its base-four representation is \(110.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: The twentieth positive number represents the ordinary value \(20\)
Divide \(20\) successively by \(4,\) or express it using the place values \(16,\) \(4,\) and \(1\)
